title: Cache Geometry Under Obfuscation
subtitle: Per-head rotation does not remove the signal, and a KV-Cloak implementation is inconclusive (v1.1 correction)
abstract: Version 1.1 (October 2026) withdraws this paper's claim that KV-Cloak defends cache-geometry methods against adversaries. Under per-head orthogonal rotation, the simulation of KV-Cloak used here, the feature that detects best without obfuscation still detects on the two models whose feature is recorded: clearly on Qwen2.5-7B (0.715 to 0.717; adjusted p < 0.001) and marginally on a distilled Qwen3.5-27B (spectral gap 0.903 to 0.787; adjusted p = 0.049). The rotation cannot change the spectrum of any single head. Under an implementation of the full KV-Cloak transform, whose parameters were not recorded, the spectral gap falls to 0.614, and after removing reply length no feature detects significantly; with seven confabulations the result is inconclusive.
